docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
The poems of Sarojini Naidu (1879–1949), poet and later president of the Indian National Congress, published in London in 1912: songs of love and death, of the Indian spring, “Indian folk-songs” of bangle-sellers, spinners, village women and the festival of serpents, and of Hyderabad, the city of her childhood. Edmund Gosse’s introduction tells how she was urged to write of India and not of English themes.

From Wikisource · Public domain

Sarojini Naidu (1879–1949), The Bird of Time (William Heinemann, 1912), with an introduction by Edmund Gosse (1849–1928), as validated on English Wikisource by its contributors.
